title: Inside Mindy Kaling's 'Not Suitable for Work': The Comedy That Completes Her Autobiographical Trilogy
excerpt: The Hulu series, starring Indian-American actress Avantika Vandanapu alongside Ella Hunt, follows ambitious twenty-somethings in Manhattan and draws from Kaling's own post-college years in New York.
body:
• Mindy Kaling's new Hulu comedy 'Not Suitable for Work' premiered June 2, 2026, completing an autobiographical trilogy that includes 'Never Have I Ever' and 'Sex Lives of College Girls'
  • Indian-American actress Avantika Vandanapu co-stars as Abhinaya "Abby" Chilukuri, an aspiring celebrity stylist — a rare South Asian lead in a major streaming comedy
  • The nine-episode series is set in Manhattan's Murray Hill and follows five work-obsessed twenty-somethings at an investment bank
  • Reviews have been mixed, but the show has drawn comparisons to 'Friends' and 'Sex and the City' for its ensemble energy

The Third Chapter

Mindy Kaling has spent a decade building the most distinctive Indian-American voice in television comedy. With 'Not Suitable for Work,' streaming on Hulu since June 2, she closes what she calls a trilogy drawn from her own life.

'Never Have I Ever' captured her high school years. 'Sex Lives of College Girls' reflected her time at Dartmouth. This latest series tackles "the last pivotal time in my youth, which was moving to New York City, being super ambitious," as Kaling explained during a 'Good Morning America' appearance.

The premise follows five work-obsessed twenty-somethings navigating careers, friendships, and romance in Manhattan's Murray Hill neighborhood. The professional anchor is Fisher Stassen, a prestigious investment bank where long hours and cutthroat ambition are table stakes.

Avantika Takes a Leading Role

The cast is led by Ella Hunt as AJ Pascarelli, a first-year analyst at the firm. But for diaspora audiences, the standout casting is Avantika Vandanapu as Abhinaya "Abby" Chilukuri, AJ's best friend and roommate who is pursuing a career as a celebrity stylist.

Avantika, who previously appeared in 'Mean Girls' (2024), brings a naturalistic charm to a character that sidesteps the usual stereotypes. Abby is ambitious, fashion-forward, and defined by her own aspirations rather than serving as a cultural foil. It's the kind of South Asian representation that Kaling's shows have consistently delivered — characters who happen to be Indian rather than characters whose Indianness is the joke.

The ensemble also includes Jay Ellis as a managing director, Will Angus as a finance workaholic, and Nicholas Duvernay (from 'The White Lotus' Season 3) as a med-school student. Gigi Hadid makes her acting debut in a guest role.

Mixed Reviews, Loyal Audience

Critical reception has been divided. Some reviewers have praised the show's warmth and ensemble chemistry, drawing comparisons to 'Friends' for its group dynamic and 'Sex and the City' for its New York ambition. Others have found the workplace comedy territory overly familiar, with one Slant Magazine review calling it "about as fun as a long day at the office."

But Kaling's track record suggests the show will find its audience. Her previous series have built devoted followings that transcend initial critical reception, particularly among South Asian viewers who see their experiences reflected on screen. 'Not Suitable for Work' is produced by Kaling International in association with Warner Bros. Television, with showrunner Charlie Grandy, a veteran of both 'The Mindy Project' and 'Sex Lives of College Girls.'
